llm.summary: This skill is a local CloudArc benchmarking workflow with disclosed repository edits and benchmark execution, and I found no hidden credential use, persistence, network retrieval, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: Local subprocess benchmark execution and filesystem writes are proportionate for a benchmark helper; manual large runs require an explicit --yes because they may consume hours and tens of GiB of temporary disk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is described as cloning into the skills directory or installing by ClawHub slug; no install-time scripts, dependency downloads, hooks, services, or remote payload execution were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill gives broad workflow instructions to inspect and update CloudArc repository files, but it also scopes activity to the repository, prohibits Downloads/source-material edits, cloud credential connection, proprietary packages, and normal PR execution of 10 GiB runs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No cross-session persistence, memory writes, tool hijacking, scheduled tasks, privilege escalation, credential storage, or background workers were found; persistent outputs are expected benchmark reports, docs, and optional badge files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is benchmarking CloudArc large-package behavior, telemetry, CI gates, and documentation; the file reads, repo-local edits, tests, benchmark runs, JSON/Markdown artifacts, and helper commands align with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only for CloudArc benchmark and telemetry work. Run the manual profile only when you intentionally want a large local benchmark, since it can take hours and use substantial temporary disk. Review output paths for generated JSON, Markdown, and badge files, but no evidence suggests credential access, network activation, or hidden persistence.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill does not declare a formal permissions block, but the artifact text itself narrows the workflow to CloudArc repo-local inspection, edits, tests, and benchmark artifacts, with explicit prohibitions on Downloads edits, cloud credentials, cloud services, and proprietary packages.
[EA2] expected: The cited text tells the agent to check skipped file counts before treating pack/analyze as complete; it is a safety check, not autonomous destructive or high-impact decision-making.
[AST4] expected: The helper uses subprocess.run with explicit argument lists and shell=False by default to invoke known Python benchmark/test commands inside a user-specified repository; this is expected for a benchmark runner.
[TT2] expected: The badge command renders SVG from a parsed benchmark result and writes it to a user-specified output path; this is a disclosed optional artifact write, not exfiltration or hidden mutation.
[SQP-2] expected: The badge output creates parent directories and writes the requested file; the README and CLI help identify it as rendering a badge, though users should choose the output path carefully.
